To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the STBA (Pseudomonas fluorescens and Bacillus subtilis) can be used as a biocontrol agent against phytopathogenic fungi of mustard crop under saline condition.

(i) the STBA can be used for the management of phytopathogen in mustard crop, (ii) the STBA is a promising candidate for the management of Sclerotinia blight of mustard crop, (iii) the STBA has the potential to reduce the use of chemical pesticide, (iv) the STBA may have the potential to be used as a plant growth promoter.
the salt tolerant biocontrol agent isolated from saline soils can be used to control phytopathogen of mustard crop.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most effective and efficient STBAs against mustard pathogens.
the development of a salt tolerance biocontrol agent (STBA) from a salt tolerant fungus, Trichoderma sp., for the control of mustard wilt disease.
the identification of the salt tolerant biocontrol agent (STBA) for the management of mustard seedling disease caused by Alternaria brassicae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the STBA (Pseudomonas sp. and Bacillus sp.) are the potential candidates for the bio-control of the fungal phytopathogens.
, in the present study, the biocontrol agents were found to have a potential role in the management of phytopathogen and the results obtained in this study are encouraging and promising.

the present study has revealed the existence of a number of salt tolerant biocontrol agent (STBA) which can be used for the control of phytopathogen and for the enhancement of mustard crop productivity under salt affected areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the salt tolerance bio control agent (STBA) isolated from the rhizospheric soil of salt affected area of Rajasthan (India) has shown promising result against the phytopathogen of mustard crop.
we have successfully isolated the STBA and found that they have the potential to inhibit the pathogenicity of mustard phytopathogen.
the STBA can be used as an alternative for the chemical pesticides to control the phytopathogen in mustard crop and can be further used as biofertilizers for the mustard crop.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of salt and drought stresses has a synergistic effect on the plant.
the salt-tolerant bacteria we identified can potentially be used in the future to develop biocontrol agents for use in agriculture.

the combination of a salt-tolerant strain of P. fluorescens (Pf-CL1) and a salt-sensitive strain of B. thuringiensis (Bt-CL1) can be used as a biopesticide to control Sclerotinia sclerotiorum in mustard under saline conditions.
